;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[Turkish military intervention in the Second Libyan Civil War]]
***A [[Turkish Naval Forces]] [[warship]] launches missiles at [[Libyan National Army|LNA]] positions near the city of [[Ajaylat]] in western [[Libya]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200401-libya-turkey-warship-fires-missiles-on-sites-controlled-by-haftar-militias/ (Middle East Monitor)]
***[[Government of National Accord|GNA]] forces say they shot down a [[CAIG Wing Loong|Wing Loong]] drone used by the LNA over Ajaylat as clashes continue. [https://www.libyaobserver.ly/news/libyan-army-downs-uae-drone-western-region (Libya Observer)]

;Business and economy
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[Hobby Lobby]] is expected to reopen in states with stay-at-home orders. [https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/hobby-lobby-open-essential-business-stay-at-home-orders/ (CBS News)]
*[[Whiting Petroleum Corporation]] declares [[bankruptcy]]. Whiting was once the largest oil producer in the [[Bakken formation|Bakken shale region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-whiting-petrol-bankruptcy/whiting-files-for-chapter-11-bankruptcy-as-oil-prices-hover-at-20-idUSKBN21J5KS (Reuters)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
**Federal authorities charge 44-year-old Eduardo Moreno, a [[railroad engineer]], with train-wrecking after he allegedly [[train derailment|derailed]] a train near [[USNS Mercy (T-AH-19)|USNS ''Mercy'']] to bring attention to the [[U.S. government]]'s response to the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/feds-charge-man-who-intentionally-derailed-train-near-usns-mercy-n1174461 (NBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] reports 130 [[Asymptomatic carrier|asymptomatic]] cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. This is its first time reporting asymptomatic cases. [https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2020-04-01/china-reports-130-asymptomatic-cases-of-coronavirus-in-one-day (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]]i Health Minister [[Yaakov Litzman]] tests positive for COVID-19 and will go into [[quarantine]], as total number of cases in Israel rises to 6,092. [https://www.jpost.com/Breaking-News/Health-Minister-Yaacvov-Litzman-diagnosed-with-coronavirus-623267 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yemen]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on prisons]]
****[[Yemen]]'s internationally recognised [[government of Yemen|government]] releases more than 470 prisoners from detention facilities in areas under its control amid growing concerns the virus could spread in Yemen's overcrowded jails. The [[United Nations Human Rights Council]] has called for the release of all political prisoners. [https://www.thenational.ae/world/mena/hundreds-of-prisoners-in-yemen-freed-amid-coronavirus-pandemic-1.1000483 (The National)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba]]
****The [[Government of Cuba|government]] announces that all flights to and from the island nation are suspended, as of midnight on April 1. [https://wsvn.com/news/us-world/cuba-will-suspend-all-international-flights-starting-at-midnight/ (WSVN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]] 
*****[[List of governors of Florida|Governor]] [[Ron DeSantis]] issues a [[stay-at-home order]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/florida-governor-issues-stay-home-order-after-weeks-resistance-n1174146 (NBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] extends its [[2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown|lockdown]] to April 13. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-italy-lockdown-idUSKBN21J4RU (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Department of Health and Social Care]] reports 563 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest daily death toll in the country to date, bringing the country's death toll to 2,352 and 29,474 cases. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52122761 (BBC News)]
****[[Chief Minister of the Isle of Man|Chief Minister]] [[Howard Quayle]] confirms the [[Isle of Man]]'s first death from COVID-19, a patient with underlying health conditions at [[Noble’s Hospital]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-isle-of-man-52126179 (BBC News)]
****Former [[List of prime ministers of Somalia|Prime Minister of Somalia]] [[Nur Hassan Hussein]] dies from COVID-19 in [[London]]. [https://www.voanews.com/science-health/coronavirus-outbreak/former-somali-pm-dies-coronavirus-london (Voice of America)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 509 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the country's death toll to 4,032 and 56,989 cases, with 6,017 of those patients reported in a serious condition requiring life support. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-france-toll/france-passes-4000-coronavirus-deaths-no-end-of-lockdown-in-sight-idUSKBN21J6JP (Reuters)]

**[[Russia]] is expected to send a plane with masks and medical supplies to the [[United States]] to help fight the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/04/01/russia-sends-medical-supplies-coronavirus-159009 (''Politico'')]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[President of the United States|United States President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that [[United States Navy]] ships will be deployed to [[Venezuela]] on an anti-drug mission. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/ap-sources-us-deploy-anti-drug-ships-venezuela-69921867 (ABC News)]
